rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although reports identify those rushing into disbelief as hypocrites, apostates, Quraysh, or Jewish leaders, the preferred reading is general, as in the warning to the Messenger in 5:41.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في المنافقين. وقيل: نزلت في قوم ارتدوا. وقيل: المراد كفار قريش. وقيل: رؤساء اليهود. والأولى حمله على العموم كقوله: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cause of the Prophet's grief was his compassion and wish to save them from the Fire by their conversion; he is told not to grieve excessively, as in 35:8 and 26:3.
rows.anchor: وإيثاره إسلامهم حتى ينقذهم من النار، فنهي عن المبالغة في ذلك كقوله تعالى: فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات وقوله: لعلك باخع نفسك ألا يكونوا مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads يحزنك from أحزن wherever the present form occurs, except لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر, which he reads like the other readers from حزن.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع: يحزنك من أحزن، وكذا حيث وقع المضارع، إلا في لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر، فقرأه من حزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs distinguish being saddened from causing sadness: حزن الرجل means sadness befell him, while حزنته and أحزنته mean he made another sad.
rows.anchor: يقال: حزن الرجل أصابه الحزن، وحزنته جعلت فيه ذلك، وأحزنته جعلته حزينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammarian reads يسرعون from أسرع throughout the Qur'an; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the majority reading يسارعون is stronger because competing to hurry implies more effort than hurrying alone.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النحوي: يسرعون من أسرع في جميع القرآن. قال ابن عطية: وقراءة الجماعة أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rush into disbelief cannot harm God; its consequence returns to them, and شيئا is an accusative cognate object meaning any amount of harm.
rows.anchor: وفي ضمن قوله: إنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا دلالة على أن وبال ذلك عائد عليهم، ولا يضرون إلا أنفسهم. وانتصب شيئا على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses شيئا as though a preposition meaning 'of' had been omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: انتصابه على إسقاط حرف الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills that these disbelievers receive no share of the afterlife: they are not guided to faith, and their deprivation is a consolation to the Prophet concerning their fate.
rows.anchor: بين تعالى أن ما هم عليه من المسارعة في الكفر هو بإرادة الله تعالى، أنهم لا يهديهم إلى الإيمان، فيكون لهم نصيب من نعيم الآخرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the mention of divine willing signals that no countervailing consideration remains to avert their deprivation and punishment as they persist in extreme rebellion.
rows.anchor: فائدته الإشعار بأن الداعي إلى حرمانهم وتعذيبهم قد خلص خلوصا لم يبق معه صارف قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's explanation carries a Muʿtazilite implication: it treats their unbelief as the cause willed by God, so he redirects the will to withholding mercy because of their extreme unbelief.
rows.anchor: وفيه دسيسة اعتزال لأنه استشعر أن إرادته تعالى أن لا يجعل لهم حظا في الآخرة موجبة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī gives three readings of God's willing: decreeing their fate; intending to deprive them of reward because disbelief nullifies deeds; or nullifying deeds for deserved sins, the last attributed to Ibn Isḥāq.
rows.anchor: ونقل الماوردي في يريد ثلاثة أقوال: أحدها: أنه يحكم بذلك. والثاني: يريد في الآخرة أن يحرمهم ثوابهم لإحباط أعمالهم بكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that those who exchanged faith for disbelief cannot harm God is general about all disbelievers; repeating the earlier warning is emphasis if that warning was general.
rows.anchor: إن الذين اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان لن يضروا الله شيئا ولهم عذاب أليم هذا عام في الكفار كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the earlier warning concerned particular hypocrites, apostates, or Quraysh, this verse includes them within a general judgment rather than merely repeating it; they receive both great and painful punishment.
rows.anchor: فيكون ليس تكريرا على سبيل التأكيد، بل حكم على العام بأنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their action is called a purchase because they could choose good or evil and preferred disbelief to faith.
rows.anchor: وجعل ذلك اشتراء. من حيث تمكنهم من قبول الخير والشر، فآثروا الكفر على الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb نملي means to give respite and extend life; ملاءة denotes a span of time and الملوان the night and day.
rows.anchor: معنى نملي: نمهل ونمد في العمر. والملاءة المدة من الدهر، والملوان الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads تحسبن with second-person tāʾ, making الذين كفروا the first object; several grammatical parses are proposed for the ensuing clause because it cannot straightforwardly be the second object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة تحسبن بتاء الخطاب، فيكون الذين كفروا مفعولا أول. ولا يجوز أن يكون: أنما نملي لهم خير، في موضع المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Bādhish and al-Zamakhsharī parse أنما نملي لهم as a substitute for الذين كفروا, with the second object omitted; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ had already proposed this parsing.
rows.anchor: وخرجه الأستاذ أبو الحسن بن الباذش والزمخشري: على أن يكون أنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم بدل من الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers construing the two clauses as repetition and emphasis: do not suppose the disbelievers, and do not suppose that respite is good for them.
rows.anchor: فالأوجه هذه القراءة التكرير والتأكيد. التقدير: ولا تحسبن الذين كفروا، ولا تحسبن أنما نملي لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians reject al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ's omission of the second object as impermissible; the author notes the dispute over omitting an object of ظن, which most allow only rarely and which Ibn Malikūn rejects.
rows.anchor: وقد رد بعضهم قول الكسائي والفراء فقال: حذف المفعول الثاني من هذه الأفعال لا يجوز عند أحد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj supports the substitute parsing for a reported reading with خير in the accusative, comparing the second هلك in a line of poetry as a substitute for the first.
rows.anchor: وعلى البدل خرج هذه القراءة أبو إسحاق الزجاج، لكن ظاهر كلامه أنها بنصب خير

rows.speaker: ابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Mujāhid rejects the reading reported by al-Zajjāj and says nobody read it; the author treats Ibn Mujāhid as the authority in Qur'anic readings.
rows.anchor: وأنكر أبو بكر بن مجاهد هذه القراءة التي حكاها الزجاج، وزعم أنه لم يقرأ بها أحد. وابن مجاهد في باب القراءات هو المرجوع إليه

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim reports al-Akhfash's objection that using the reading for the Qadarites is ugly; al-Akhfash instead fronts and delays clauses, making the first إملاء clause the second object and the other a sentence.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: سمعت الأخفش يذكر قبح أن يحتج بها لأهل القدر

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says إنما must have a kasra in this reading, with إن and its clause functioning as the two-object complement.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: ينبغي أن تكون الألف من إنما مكسورة في هذه القراءة

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī says he knows no one who read تحسبن with tāʾ and a kasra in إنما.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي في مشكله: ما علمت أحدا قرأ تحسبن بالتاء من فوق، وكسر الألف من إنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading uses third-person يحسبن; its syntax is straightforward because أنما نملي لهم خير fills both objects, like 'I thought that Zayd was standing.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة والجمهور يحسبن بالياء، وإعراب هذه القراءة ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In either reading, ما may be a relative pronoun with an omitted resumptive or a verbal noun meaning 'our granting respite.'
rows.anchor: وتحتمل ما في هذه القراءة وفي التي قبلها أن تكون موصولة بمعنى الذي، ومصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some allow the verb's subject to be the Prophet, making the two readings equivalent in meaning; Yahyā ibn Waththāb reads the verb in the third person and إنما with kasra, producing a remote hanging construction if the disbelievers are its subject.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يسند الفعل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reports Yahyā's first إنما with kasra and second with fatḥa, taking the latter as an interruption: respite is good for them if they use it to repent and recognize God's favor.
rows.anchor: وحكى الزمخشري أن يحيى بن وثاب قرأ بكسر إنما الأولى، وفتح الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb is parsed as a hanging clause with kasra, although the expected lām is outside its scope.
rows.anchor: فخرج على ذلك التعليق فكسرت إن، وإن لم تكن اللام في حيزها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about Jews, Christians, and hypocrites; ʿAṭāʾ says it concerns Qurayẓa and Naḍīr, while Muqātil says Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في اليهود والنصارى والمنافقين. وقال عطاء: في قريظة والنضير. وقال مقاتل: في مشركي مكة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says these are people God informed the Prophet would never believe, not every disbeliever, since respite may lead another person to faith; Makkī calls this the correct interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هؤلاء قوم أعلم الله نبيه أنهم لا يؤمنون أبدا، وليست في كل كافر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reads the verse as rebutting disbelievers who take their worldly prominence and wealth as proof that God approves their way: their delay is a reprieve that lets sins grow.
rows.anchor: معنى هذه الآية الرد على الكفار في قولهم: إن كوننا ظاهرين ممولين أصحة دليل على رضا الله بحالنا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says death is better for every righteous or wicked person: the righteous hasten to mercy and the wicked avoid further sins, citing 3:198 and this verse.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: ما من نفس برة ولا فاجرة إلا والموت خير لها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains respite as giving them rein, like loosening a horse's lead, or simply prolonging their lives; the next clause independently explains why they think it benefits them.
rows.anchor: والإملاء لهم تحليتهم، وشأنهم مستعار من أملى لفرسه إذا أرخى له الطول ليرعى كيف شاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says increasing sin is a cause of respite rather than God's intended goal; because God knows their sins will increase, the respite is figuratively said to occur for that reason.
rows.anchor: هو علة الإملاء، وما كل علة بغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Zamakhsharī's account follows the Muʿtazilite way.
rows.anchor: وكله جار على طريقة المعتزلة

rows.speaker: الماتريدي
rows.claim: Al-Māturīdī reports two Muʿtazilite parses: fronting the 'increase in sin' clause, or describing their mistaken belief that worldly respite and prosperity will yield a good final outcome; he criticizes the second as an implausible warning to the already knowledgeable.
rows.anchor: المعتزلة تناولوها على وجهين: أحدهما: على التقديم والتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribes joined ما to أن in both places in the codex; although separation would suit the first by grammatical analogy, the written codex is followed, and the second ما is a particle, not a relative or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وكتبوا ما متصلة بأن في الموضعين. قيل: وكان القياس الأولى في علم الخط أن تكتب مفصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ليزدادوا may indicate consequence rather than purpose.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللام في ليزدادوا للصيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the lām in ليزدادوا indicates consequence rather than purpose.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللام في ليزدادوا للصيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes the waw circumstantial to reconcile the reading with his preferred sense, but the transmitted reading does not establish the second fatḥa he needs.
rows.anchor: ولكن الزمخشري من ولوعه بنصرة مذهبه يروم رد كل شيء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is called great because rushing to attain something suggests it is highly prized; the great punishment underscores the worthlessness of what they pursued.
rows.anchor: فختمت الآية بعظم الثواب وهو جزاؤهم على المسارعة في الكفر إشعارا بخساسة ما سابقوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Painful punishment suits the image of buying disbelief for faith: a buyer usually rejoices in a purchase, but a ruined bargain brings pain.
rows.anchor: فختمت الآية لأن صفقته خسرت بألم العذاب، كما يجده المشتري المغبون في تجارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humiliating punishment suits respite that gave them wealth, health, and status: the worldly pride ends in humiliation before punishment.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا الإمتاع سببا للتعزز والتمتع والاستطاعة فختمت الآية بإهانة العذاب لهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One reading addresses believers mixed with hypocrites: God would not leave them indistinguishable, and their statements and actions reveal the difference; this is attributed to Mujāhid, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Isḥāq.
rows.anchor: قاله: مجاهد، وابن جريج، وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: An alternative addresses disbelievers mixed with believers; Qatāda and al-Suddī attribute this reading, in a context where disbelievers challenge how a follower can change from hellbound to destined for Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخطاب للكفار، والمعنى: على ما أنتم عليه أيها الكفار من اختلاطكم بالمؤمنين قاله: قتادة، والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most commentators take the address as aimed at disbelievers and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وأكثر المفسرين الخطاب للكفار والمنافقين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers a broad address to sincere and hypocritical professing believers: revelation distinguishes the sincere from those who had shared their outward profession.
rows.anchor: للمصدقين جميعا من أهل الإخلاص والنفاق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The author says the distinction becomes visible through the two groups’ outward statements and actions.
rows.anchor: بما ظهر من هؤلاء وهؤلاء من الأقوال والأفعال

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysān explains that God does not leave people at mere profession but tests them through religious laws and obligations.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: المعنى ما يذركم على الإقرار حتى يختبركم بالشرائع والتكاليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported interpretations say God separates believing children from their polytheist parents, exposes secret mockery and hypocrisy through trial, or separates people in the afterlife into Hell and Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ما كان الله ليذر أولادكم الذين حكم عليهم بالإيمان على ما أنتم عليه من الشرك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the pure as believers and the corrupt as hypocrites, distinguished at Uḥud.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الطيب المؤمن، والخبيث المنافق، ميز بينهما يوم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify the corrupt and pure as disbeliever and believer, separated by birth from one another, or as sinners and obedient people; trials may also remove believers' sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخبيث الكافر، والطيب المؤمن، وتمييزه بإخراج أحدهما من صلب الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite articles in الخبيث and الطيب can mark either a class generally or the familiar referents of disbeliever and believer, as in 24:26.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام في الخبيث والطيب للجنس أو للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, Kūfans call the lām in ليذر an emphatic extra lām that itself governs the subjunctive; Basrans posit an omitted predicate of kāna and an understood أن after a lām strengthening its demand.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله: ليذر هي المسماة لام الجحود، وهي عند الكوفيين زائدة لتأكيد النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say the verse followed a claim that wealthy people deserved revelation, or that devils once stole heavenly news for soothsayers; God alone chooses a messenger and reveals to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قالوا: نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا فهلا كان الوحي إلينا، فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that God alone distinguishes believers from hypocrites, since people are not shown the faith and hypocrisy hidden in hearts; He informs a chosen messenger, who conveys it by revelation.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية هو ما قدمناه من أنه تعالى هو الذي يميز بين الخبيث والطيب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says God decreed that this distinction would be made manifest; common people cannot label individuals by unseen knowledge, but can know through testing, while prophets may be informed by revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى ما روي أيضا عن السدي أنه قال: حكم بأنه يظهر هذا التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen distinction may also be read broadly: God does not make all people as knowledgeable of hidden matters as the messenger, whom He alone chooses to inform.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك على سبيل العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing in God and His messengers follows the mention of God's selecting a messenger and revealing hidden matters; Muhammad is intended, and his reports of unseen things establish his prophethood.
rows.anchor: والمجتبى ومن يشاء هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، إذ ثبتت نبوته بإطلاع الله إياه على المغيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'His messengers' signals that the proof of all prophets is one: miracles appearing through them.
rows.anchor: وجمع في قوله ورسله تنبيها على أن طريق إثبات نبوة جميع الأنبياء واحدة، وهو ظهور المعجز على أيديهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says believers must recognize God as sole knower of the unseen and regard messengers as chosen servants who know only what God teaches them.
rows.anchor: بأن تقدروه حق قدره، وتعلمونه وحده مطلعا على الغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great reward is attached to faith in God and His messengers and to taqwā, which is an additional duty implied in the preceding command to believe.
rows.anchor: رتب حصول الأجر العظيم على الإيمان، والمعنى: الإيمان السابق، وهو الإيمان بالله ورسله، وعلى التقوى وهي زائدة على الإيمان

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and others say the verse concerns withholding wealth and spending in God's path.
rows.anchor: قال السدي وجماعة: نزلت في البخل بالمال والإنفاق في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās in a report from ʿAṭiyya, Mujāhid, Ibn Jurayj, and others, with al-Zajjāj's preference, say it concerns People of the Book withholding what they knew about Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطية، ومجاهد وابن جريج وجماعة، واختاره الزجاج: في أهل الكتاب وبخلهم تبيان ما علمهم الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Hurayra, another Ibn ʿAbbās narration, al-Shaʿbī, and Mujāhid applies it to people withholding obligatory zakāt; another view concerns family support.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في مانعي الزكاة المفروضة قاله: ابن مسعود، وأبو هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows exhortation to sacrifice lives in jihad with exhortation to spend wealth in jihad and elsewhere; legal miserliness is withholding what is obligatory.
rows.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى لما بالغ في التحريض على بذل الأرواح في الجهاد في الآيات السابقة، شرع في التحريض هنا على بذل الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads تحسبن with tāʾ, making الذين the first object after an understood possessive; the other readers use yāʾ and require a subject/object analysis, with an omitted first object if the misers are subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة تحسبن بالتاء، فتكون الذين أول مفعولين لتحسبن

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash omits هو, making خيرا the object of تحسبن; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says يبخلون signals the omitted noun بخلهم, though the author distinguishes this from the poetic example he cites.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش بإسقاط هو، وخيرا هو المفعول بتحسبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author offers an unusual coordination analysis: ما آتاهم is the first object sought by تحسبن while هو and خيرا are its second object; يبخلون governs the same phrase through a preposition, and the second verb is given precedence.
rows.anchor: ويظهر لي تخريج غريب في الآية تقتضيه قواعد العربية، وهو أن تكون المسألة من باب الإعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because negating that miserliness or the withheld gift is good leaves open neutrality or harm, the following clause explicitly establishes that it is harmful.
rows.anchor: وكان تحت الانتفاء قسمان: أحدهما أن لا خير ولا شر، والآخر إثبات الشر، أتى بالجملة التي تعين أحد القسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collaring is apparently figurative: they will be bound to the punishment like someone forced to wear a collar, as expressed in an Arabic proverb.
rows.anchor: والظاهر حمله على المجاز، أي سيلزمون عقابه إلزام الطوق

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī begins a literal interpretation in which they will be given a collar on the Day of Resurrection; the passage continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: سيجعل لهم يوم القيامة طوق من نار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and others take سيطوقون from الطاقة, meaning they will be made to bear the punishment of what they withheld; the author says this does not fit withholding knowledge about the Messenger.
rows.anchor: هو من الطاقة لا من التطويق، والمعنى: سيحملون عقاب ما بخلوا به

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid also says they will be required to produce the like of what they withheld.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: سيكلفون أن يأتوا بمثل ما بخلوا به

rows.speaker: أبو وائل
rows.claim: Abū Wāʾil describes a person who withholds relatives' rightful share of his wealth as being collared by a serpent that says, 'I am your wealth.'
rows.anchor: وقال أبو وائل: هو الرجل يرزقه الله مالا فيمنع منه قرابته الحق الذي جعل الله لهم في ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic hadith says a relative denied one's surplus wealth will come as a fiery serpent, licking its lips, and collar the miser; reports about withholding zakāt and hoarding are many and sound.
rows.anchor: إلا أخرج له يوم القيامة شجاع من النار يتلمظ حتى يطوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's inheritance of the heavens and earth can mean He truly owns everything attributed to creatures, so people should not hoard what they only temporarily enjoy; the verse links this to 57:7.
rows.anchor: وأنفقوا مما جعلكم مستخلفين فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase foretells the world's end: God inherits what creatures leave behind, language framed for human understanding although His ownership has always been complete.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني: أنه خبر بفناء العالم، وأن جميع ما يخلفونه فهو وارثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing description 'God is aware of what you do' threatens misers for their wrongdoing; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read the verb in the third person, while others address the misers directly, which the author calls the better reading of the shift.
rows.anchor: ختم بهذه الصفة ومعناها التهديد والوعيد على قبيح مرتكبهم من البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage's rhetorical devices include specification, repetition, antithesis, metaphor, paronomasia, shifts of address, and ellipsis; its metaphors include rushing, buying, respite, sin-increase, and pure versus corrupt.
rows.anchor: التجنيس المماثل في: فآمنوا وإن تؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in والله بما تعملون خبير is an address shift for readers of تعملون with tāʾ; the shift in أنتم depends on whom the address is understood to target.
rows.anchor: والالتفات في: أنتم إن كان خطابا للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read both يحسبن forms in the third person and رفع the bāʾ in يحسبنهم; one parse leaves the first verb without an object, while another takes the second clause as a substitute.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: لا يحسبن ولا يحسبنهم بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl notes that Arabic can use verbs of thinking without full sentence force in expressions such as 'I did not think anyone says that except Zayd.'
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل: العرب تقول: ما رأيته يقول ذلك إلا زيد، وما ظننته يقول ذلك إلا زيد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's alternative deletes the first object and makes فلا يحسبنهم confirm the sense 'do not count them as safe'; the author has elsewhere rejected this deletion analysis.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني ما قاله الزمخشري: وهو أن يكون المفعول الأول محذوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read both verbs in the third person; one parse makes the first verb objectless, and another treats the second clause as a substitute.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: لا يحسبن ولا يحسبنهم بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the first يحسبن has no object, with الذين as its subject.
rows.anchor: وهو أن لا يحسبن لم يقع على شيء، والذين رفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya parses the second clause as a substitute for the first and supplies its two objects from بمفازة.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: فتتجه القراءة بكون فلا يحسبنهم بدلا من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers a different parse that omits the first object, which the author rejects elsewhere.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني ما قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the variant associated with ʿAbd Allāh, the phrase بما لم يفعلوا بمفازة appears and فلا يحسبنهم is omitted; مفازة means a place of escape or distance from harm.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله بما لم يفعلوا بمفازة، وأسقط فلا يحسبنهم. ومفازة مفعلة من فاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim read both forms with second-person tāʾ and fatḥa, with competing analyses of their objects.
rows.anchor: لا تحسبن، وفلا تحسبنهم بتاء الخطاب، وفتح الباء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read the first verb in the third person and the second in the second person, requiring omitted objects.
rows.anchor: لا يحسبن بياء الغيبة، وفلا تحسبنهم بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī and Marwān read بما آتوا as 'what they gave'; Ibn Jubayr and al-Sulamī use the passive بما أوتوا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النخعي ومروان بن الحكم بما آتوا بمعنى: أعطوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth and alternation of night and day are clear signs of the Creator and His astonishing wisdom, apparent to people of intellect who reason and reflect.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لآيات: لعلامات واضحة على الصانع وباهر حكمته، ولا يظهر ذلك إلا لذوي العقول ينظرون في ذلك بطريق الفكر والاستدلال

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that Quraysh asked the Prophet to make Ṣafā gold after Jews and Christians mentioned Moses' miracles; this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جبير عن ابن عباس أن قريشا قالوا للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادع لنا ربك يجعل لنا الصفا ذهبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the declaration that God owns heaven and earth and is powerful, adding that their creation displays clear proofs to rational observers.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها واضحة، لأنه تعالى لما ذكر أنه مالك السموات والأرض، وذكر قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is remembrance with the tongue and an attentive heart, including praise, tahlīl, takbīr, and similar devotions; the three postures represent all circumstances.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الذكر هو باللسان مع حضور القلب، وأنه التحميد والتهليل والتكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Messenger remembered God at all times; the verse and hadith apparently permit remembrance in the lavatory, as held by Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Sīrīn, and al-Nakhaʿī, but disliked by Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Shaʿbī.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر الله على كل أحيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith encourages abundant remembrance to graze in Paradise's gardens; Ibn Jurayj and most commentators take the verse's remembrance in its ordinary sense and call it a great act of worship.
rows.anchor: من أحب أن يرتع في رياض الجنة فليكثر ذكر الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others interpret remembrance as obligatory prayers performed sitting or lying down when there is an excuse; another view specifies voluntary prayer in any posture.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وجماعة: المراد بالذكر الصلوات، ففي حال العذر يصلونها قعودا وعلى جنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the ordinary remembrance reading, standing is named first because it is easiest; sitting is more demanding, then lying down is hardest because it is a posture of rest and fewer distractions.
rows.anchor: فتقديم القيام، لأن الذكر فيه أخف على الإنسان، ثم انتقل إلى حالة القعود والذكر فيه أشق منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويتفكرون may coordinate with the relative clause without its own syntactic position, or form a circumstantial clause; remembrance belongs to the tongue, thought to the heart.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه معطوف على الصلة، فلا موضع له من الإعراب. وقيل: الجملة في موضع نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation may mean the act of creating: reflecting on these extraordinary works from nothing proves God's power, knowledge, oneness, and other exalted attributes.
rows.anchor: فإن الفكرة في الخلق لهذه المصنوعات الغريبة الشكل والقدرة على إنشاء هذه من العدم الصرف، يدل على القدرة التامة والعلم والأحدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, creation means the created things: considering the stars, spheres, animals, plants, minerals, and their diverse kinds and individuals overwhelms the mind and multiplies lessons.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد به المخلوق، ويكون أضافه من حيث المعنى إلى الظرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says to reflect on creation, not the Creator, whose true measure people cannot grasp; scholars compare contemplating God's essence to staring at the sun and direct thought to created things and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: تفكروا في الخلق ولا تفكروا في الخالق فإنكم لا تقدرون قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author omits the commentators’ many sayings about reflection to avoid making the book longer.
rows.anchor: رأينا أن لا نطول كتابنا بنقلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller is either the Messenger, as Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd say, making his call literal, or the Qur'an, as Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī says, making hearing acceptance metaphorical.
rows.anchor: والمنادى هنا هو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'a caller calling' first introduces the caller generally and then specifies that he calls to faith, magnifying him above imagined callers to war, rescue, or worldly needs.
rows.anchor: وجمع بين قوله: مناديا ينادي، لأنه ذكر الأول مطلقا وقيد الثاني تفخيما لشأن المنادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in للإيمان may mean 'to' because ندَى and دعا can govern both ل and إلى, or may mark purpose or instrument; أن آمنوا may be explanatory or a verbal noun governed by باء.
rows.anchor: واللام متعلقة بينادي، ويعدى نادى، ودعا، وندب باللام وبإلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the caller is the Prophet, hearing is literal; if it is Qur'an, hearing means acceptance. The ف in فآمنا signals prompt belief caused by hearing.
rows.anchor: وعطف فآمنا بالفاء مؤذن بتعجيل القبول، وتسبيب الإيمان عن السماع من غير تراخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petition that God give what He promised asks Him to make the petitioners steadfast in faith and obedience so they become worthy, by His mercy, of the promised reward; it may also be humble supplication despite certainty of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أنه تعالى منجز ما وعد، فسألوا إنجاز ما ترتب على الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they felt the promised victory was delayed and asked God to hasten it; on that reading the promise is fulfilled in this world, while a promise of Paradise is in the next.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استبطؤوا النصر الذي وعدوا به فسألوا أن يعجل لهم وعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads على رسلك with a still sīn; يوم القيامة may modify ولا تخزنا or, if the promise is Paradise, be governed by both the petition to grant it and the petition not to disgrace them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: على رسلك بإسكان السين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes 'You do not break the promise' as alluding to God's promise not to disgrace the Prophet and believers on Judgment Day; he infers disgrace belongs to everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله تعالى: يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their address 'our Lord' recognizes God as the one who nurtured and prepared them for worship; they state the result of reflection before asking protection from the Fire.
rows.anchor: فإنهم خاطبوا الله تعالى بلفظة ربنا، وهي إشارة إلى أنه ربهم أصلحهم وهيأهم للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who enter the Fire are wrongdoers who neither remember God nor reflect on His works; the supplicants then recount that reflection led them to answer the call to faith.
rows.anchor: وأخبروا عن حال من يدخل النار وهم الظالمون الذين لا يذكرون الله، ولا يتفكرون في مصنوعاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask forgiveness, death in faith, Paradise, and protection from disgrace at Judgment, completing the sequence of their requests.
rows.anchor: ثم سألوا غفران ذنوبهم ووفاتهم على الإيمان الذي أخبروا به في قولهم: فآمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeat 'our Lord' five times to appeal for mercy; repetition shows that persistent supplication is allowed, contrary to some Sufis and antinomian mystics.
rows.anchor: وتكرر لفظ ربنا خمس مرات، كل ذلك على سبيل الاستعطاف وتطلب رحمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they kept saying 'our Lord' until God answered them; a hadith likewise urges repeated invocation of 'Possessor of Majesty and Honor.'
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما زالوا يقولون ربنا ربنا حتى استحاب لهم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The author cites Abū Hurayra's report that the Prophet recited the last ten verses of Āl ʿImrān every night and says it is recommended for someone waking to wipe the face and begin prayer by reciting them, joining reflection with action.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ عشر آيات من آخر سورة آل عمران كل ليلة

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama asked why revelation mentioned men but not women among emigrants; this verse and related verses were revealed in response.
rows.anchor: روي أن أم سلمة قالت: يا رسول الله قد ذكر الله الرجال في الهجرة ولم يذكر النساء في شيء من ذلك، فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استجاب means 'answered' and governs a direct object or a lām phrase; a report from Tāj al-Qurrāʾ says أجاب is general while استجاب specifically implies attaining the request.
rows.anchor: ونقل تاج القراء أن أجاب عام، واستجاب خاص في حصول المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have أني with an omitted باء ('because'); Ubayy reads بأني, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads إني, explained either with an implied saying or as a quotation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بأني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read أضيع from أضاع; others use the intensified form ضيع, illustrated by a poet's line about neglecting one's own child while nursing another's.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أضيع من أضاع. وقرأ بعضهم: أضيع بالتشديد من ضيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise means God does not leave a worker's reward unpaid; منكم modifies العامل, while من ذكر أو أنثى is variously explanatory, extra after negation, circumstantial, or appositional, though the author objects to some appositional parses.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ذلك: لا أترك جزاء عامل منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The special merit of migration ended with the conquest, but its underlying meaning remains until the end of time.
rows.anchor: واسم الهجرة وفضلها الخاص قد انقطع بعد الفتح، ولكن المعنى باق إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning expulsion after migration assigns guilt to the disbelievers who forced believers out; their cruelty caused the migration, as 2:217 calls expulsion from the sanctuary a greater offense.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: أن المهاجرين إنما أخرجهم سوء عشرة الكفار وقبيح أفعالهم معهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya distinguishes forced expulsion, phrased as being driven out, from voluntarily leaving through one's own strength; the Prophet corrected Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith for claiming he had been driven out.
rows.anchor: فقال له الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence narrows first to migration to Medina, then expands to all expulsion, including migration to Abyssinia and Abū Jandal, and finally to all forms of persecution in God's religion.
rows.anchor: وبدأ أولا بالخاص وهي الهجرة وكانت تطلق على الهجرة إلى المدينة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final ascent is to fighting those responsible and martyrdom: the verse gathers the hardships of migration, expulsion, persecution, and death for religion.
rows.anchor: وارتقى بعد هذه الأوصاف السنية إلى رتبة جهاد من أخرجه ومقاومته واستشهاده في دين الله
